name: Tomas
goesBy: Ser Warrant -- 'the Warrant'. A warrant is a pledge, a guarantee; he is addressed by the very thing he embodies. It is a title, not a name, so it conceals nothing of his birth while hiding everything of it. He refuses to give his true name, Tomas, to anyone; to the dragonkin he is simply 'the knight' or 'the Warrant'.
description: A human knight of the mountain kingdom, mortal, ~34 -- squarely mid-life. A guarantor-knight (see the-kingdom / human-faith-and-magic): not chiefly a warrior but the crown's living surety, whose faith-sealed word is the kingdom's bond. Disciplined, correct, self-contained -- a man who cannot afford a single misstep, because everything he is was earned and could be lost. Beneath the composure: a buried longing, a deep loneliness, and the wariness of one who climbed out of bondage and never quite believes the climb is safe.
backstory: Born a bonded servant -- a near-serf owned to a lord, the lowest rung of the realm. Knighthood freed him, and freed him by its very nature: a bonded man's word is not his own and so cannot be surety, therefore swearing the guarantor's faith-oath (a real binding of the triune god) must make him free. His liberty and his word are one and the same act. The oath gave him, all at once, his freedom, a station, and a name of his own choosing -- Ser Warrant -- while he buried his given name, Tomas, the last relic of the bonded boy he was. As a young man he loved a woman truly and was truly loved; they meant to bond for life. But their stones never glowed for one another, and in time he watched hers blaze for another man. He took the lesson that his own heart could not be trusted -- only the stone's verdict -- tucked that part of himself away, and gave his years to the oath. Until, against everything he had come to believe, a bond-stone blazes for a cursed dragonkin.
theBonding: During the stay, Tomas and Soraya are soul-bonded by the marriage rite (see human-faith-and-magic). To bond a dragonkin his body is remade utterly in a metaphysical trial of unyielding pain, and he must shed Ser Warrant to accept himself as nobody-Tomas and his bride as she is. At the trial's end he glimpses the spirit of the slain progenitor and is assaulted by the curse, which partially damages the bond. He emerges transformed and liminal -- no longer wholly human: gifted with Soraya's earth and doomed green, imperfectly long-lived, bearing an imperfect share of the curse, and sharing her senses and abilities. Because the bond is damaged, her death would leave him catastrophically, permanently wounded rather than dead. Leaning: the damage spared him the curse's operative doom, so he can still return to Marrenhold -- remade, part-cursed, and never whole.
motivation: WANT: fulfill his charge, keep his oath, and preserve the self he built -- the freedom, name, and personhood the knighthood gave a man who was born owning none of them. NEED: to reclaim the heart he buried; to be a person and not a function; to trust his own heart again and believe he is worthy of love. The tragedy is that want and need become mutually exclusive, and the stone's blaze is what forces the collision.
arc: From a man who is only his oath -- homeless, heart buried, sure the stone denied him love -- reawakened among the dragonkin into a person with a heart, a name, and, for the first time, a home, a people, and a wife. Then the war-summons forces the choice, and his defining virtue becomes his fatal flaw: the fidelity that made him refuses Soraya's plea to stay, and he chooses the oath and leaves. On the road the bond tears -- she is dying -- and he turns back at last, but forsaking the summons breaks the oath and unmakes him. He arrives too late to a slaughtered fold and finds her body last. Forsworn, unmade, and maimed by the severed bond, he is left among the ash with everything lost -- love, people, oath, and self -- his reversal a heartbeat too late. The man who had nothing, found everything, and by keeping faith destroyed it all.
traits: honest -- his word is his being

relationships.The dragonkin love interest (TBD): The woman whose deliberate clasp lights his long-dead stone; the one person to whom he will finally give his true name.
relationships.The king: His honorable liege. The king's genuine worthiness is what makes the oath so hard to break -- the duty owed him is real, not hollow.
relationships.The squire: His trusted second, sent with the caravan to fetch the crown's resources. The squire's long ride is the ticking clock of the whole story; the bond between them matters (protege, near-son).
relationships.The tribe-leader: His captor-host through the guarantor period -- wary respect between two men each keeping faith for their people.
relationships.The first love: The woman whose stone stayed dark with his, then lit for another man. Backstory only -- she does not appear; her leaving is the wound that taught him to trust the stone over his own heart.

openQuestions: Exact byname aside, few remain: whether his knighting involved a specific patron or was purely oath-by-manumission (currently the latter); the first love's name, if ever needed.
